kill_reason: Not a kill, but the assortment half of this category is near-dead and must be reported as such. The coverage diff itself returned mustHaveMissing: [] — 0 of 52 researched lines missing, 44.2% specific / 55.8% broad matches. My independent probes confirmed only four genuine absences, and three of them should NOT be added: sourdough/artisan (probe: 0 SKUs, but ARY's best-selling loaf is a Rs 30 atta bread — a Rs 140-250 loaf with a 2-5 day shelf life at 1,551 m will be written off); cake mix (probe: 1 SKU, Pillsbury Egg Free Chocolate, NEVER sold — the campus buys finished Rs 200-400 birthday cakes from its own bakery, Rs 1.55 L/yr, and hostels have no ovens); baby/toddler biscuits & teething rusks, which the demand research calls "must-have" (probe teething farex cerelac nestum slurrp timios = 34 SKUs but ALL in Food Supplement > Cerelac, Rs 3,878/12m — and the vault's VERIFIED 425 diaper packs + 13 formula packs a year means 1-2 infants on the entire campus; this is a structural zero, not a gap). Two more research lines are ALREADY_COVERED and were nearly mis-called: the "Rs 5/Rs 10 impulse biscuit rack" is not a gap, it is ARY's core biscuit business — 129 SKUs in the Rs 6-10 band carrying 70.7% of biscuit units and 47.7% of biscuit value; and "burger buns / pizza base", which look like Rs 1.5 L of dead stock (Leela Burger 4 Pcs: 1,298 bought, 2 sold, 329 on hand), are actually canteen INPUTS — Stock shows Pur 1,298 -> TrIn 1,317 into Ary G Canteen -> Cons/Sho, feeding Burger Gc at Rs 4.22 L with Prod 36,147. Recommending those would be worse than useless.
penetration_assumption: Every number below is ESTIMATED from a VERIFIED live base rate; none assumes new demand. (1) Khari & fan Rs 30,000/yr: khari competes for the same tea-accompaniment occasion as rusk, so I anchor on rusk's OBSERVED rate — rusk sold 2,716 units / Rs 58,460 in 12m = 0.58 units per resident per year. Khari is fresh (needs a daily bake) versus rusk's shelf-stable pack, so I take HALF that rate: 0.29 units x 4,700 residents = 1,363 packs, plus an impulse-counter share on the Lmk Pts counter (which moves 25,314 units/yr), rounded to ~2,000 packs at Rs 15 = Rs 30,000. (2) Lmk Pts patties Rs 30,000/yr: NOT a penetration assumption at all — it is recovery of a measured outage. Purchases were 2,400-3,000 units every month except July 2026 = ZERO, and October 2025 = 1,570. Recovering July at the 11-month mean (Rs 22,000 of sales) plus October's shortfall (Rs 8,400) = Rs 30,000. Winter-shutdown days (29 Dec - 20 Jan, campus empty, 8 selling days in Jan) are EXCLUDED as legitimate, not counted as lost. (3) Dry cake Rs 37,000/yr: on shelf only 94 of 354 open days, earning Rs 703/day when present. Moving it to a realistic weekly-order 200 days (not 354) = +106 days x Rs 703 = Rs 74,500; I halve it to Rs 37,000 because packaged cake/slice is available 96% of days and absorbs part of the demand. (4) Buns Rs 8,000, bread Rs 6,000, rusk Rs 4,000: missing-days x Rs/day when present, then halved for substitution — bread is the clearest case, available 343/354 days, so only 11 zero-bread days x 14.5 loaves x Rs 39.5 = Rs 6,300 is genuinely lost. (5) Bread crumbs Rs 4,000/yr: anchored on ARY's existing cooking-aid cluster, which does Rs 4,293/yr combined (Weikfield custard Rs 1,968 + three baking powders Rs 2,325). Population denominator 4,700 term-time (vault Population.md: 4,550-4,800; permanent winter base only 1,700-2,300).

RESTOCK, do not add — Lmk Pts (Rs 9 patty, ProductID in Bakery Items>Bread): ARY's #1 bakery SKU, Rs 2,27,826 and 25,314 units at 44.7% live margin and ZERO GST. Bought 0 units in July 2026 vs 2,400-3,000 every other month, during the Hygienic Milk -> Akal Bakery account handover. Fix = a standing daily order, not a catalogue change. Rs 30,000/yr recoverable, Rs 13,410 gross profit — the single largest item in this whole category.

RESTOCK — rusk: 44 active SKUs but only 9 ever sell; June 2026 dropped to 16 selling days and July to 21, against 28-31 normal. Hold 3 working SKUs (Parle Rusk 100+9g, Parle Rusk 200g Premium, Britannia Rusk 100+34g) year-round rather than listing 44.

DELIST candidate — 663 of 987 active bakery SKUs sold nothing in 12 months and only 13 of them hold any stock. This is a phantom catalogue, not dead capital; delisting frees no money but would make the reorder report readable.
blockers: The whole opportunity is Rs 1.19 lakh of revenue and Rs 31,000 of gross profit against a Rs 7.67 Cr business — 0.155% of turnover. It does not deserve a project. It deserves one conversation with Akal Bakery and a reorder rule.

Reorder discipline is the actual blocker, not supply. The Rs 9 patty is BAKED ON CAMPUS by a Trust-owned unit that ARY already buys from 121 times a year, and it still went unordered for a full month. No sourcing, freight or capital problem explains that.

Supplier-account continuity: purchases from the campus bakery/dairy unit fell from Rs 2-3 lakh/month (Sep-May, under 'Hygienic Milk') to Rs 30,958 / Rs 12,608 / Rs 30,097 in Jun/Jul/Aug (under 'Akal Bakery - Baru Sahib'). Part of that drop is non-bakery items (Loose Desi Ghee Rs 9.9 L, Lmk Gas Rs 3.4 L) that may have moved to another account rather than stopped — I did NOT verify where they went, so do not read the whole fall as a supply collapse.

Akal Bakery is ARY's own Trust's unit and its CREDITOR, not a vendor to squeeze. The vault (Ten-Moves move 1) is explicit: do not open with a quote. A khari/fan request is a recipe ask on an existing delivery run, which is why it is cheap; it is not a procurement negotiation.

Shelf life and hill logistics kill the premium lines outright. Fresh bread is 2-5 days at ambient and mould, not staling, is the loss driver at PIN 173101. Every artisan/sourdough/gourmet line the research proposes fails on this plus price — ARY's top loaf is Rs 30.

Population is shrinking, not growing: EU enrolment 1,102 (flat for 10 years, 51.6% seat fill), Akal Academy Grade XII down 50% since 2018-19. And 23 winter days run at 35-39% of term volume with a permanent base of only 1,700-2,300. Any bakery plan that assumes growth is planning against a falling denominator.

Biscuit margin is structurally thin — 10.2% net of GST live, versus the 12-25% the demand research assumed. Rusk is 8.2%. There is no margin case for deepening packaged biscuits; the only good margins in this category are the own-bake lines (patties 44.7%, bread subgroup 26.8%).

Confidence limiter on the availability numbers: FusionERP8 stores no daily stock snapshot (Stock rows are period aggregates, and ProductMaster.QuantityOnHand is dead), so I used sale-days as a proxy for in-stock days. That proxy is strong for daily lines like bread and patties and weak for slow movers. The Lmk Pts July finding does NOT rest on the proxy — purchases and sales independently both read zero.

Khari volume is anchored on a substitute (rusk), not on observed khari demand anywhere on this campus. It is the softest number in this report. A two-week trial at one counter would settle it for the cost of the stock.
